title: Factorization of the actual completed-pullback comparison through the limit mate
statement:
Let $g:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Fix a Noetherian adic datum $(A,I)$, $P_n=A/I^n$ for $n\ge1$, and $B_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$ for $T=X,Y$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Assume the projection-defined coefficient map $c_g:g^{-1}B_X\to B_Y$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] is an isomorphism. Use module sheaves, their unbounded derived categories and strict inverse sequences [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-inverse-system].

Put $F(M)=g^{-1}M\otimes_{g^{-1}B_X,c_g}B_Y$, and assume $F$ is additive and exact. Let $F_D:D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))\to D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_Y))$ and $F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}$ be exact termwise pullback, identified with the specified left-derived functors by their original universal counits as in [lem-sf-exact-pullback-counit-normalization]. Fix the canonical constant-tower/total-right-derived-limit adjunctions $\Delta_T\dashv L_T$, with unit $v_T$ and counit $\varepsilon_T$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit, lem-coef-derived-tower-counit-projections]. Let $j:F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}\Delta_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\Delta_YF_D$ be the identification induced from equality on ordinary constant towers and those counit-normalized comparisons. For a derived strict tower $M$ define its right mate
$$\beta_M=L_Y(F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}\varepsilon_{X,M})\,L_Y(j_{L_XM}^{-1})\,v_{Y,F_DL_XM}.$$
For $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$ let $i_K:\Delta_XK\to K_\bullet$ be its strict quotient augmentation, and put $\operatorname{comp}_K=L_X(i_K)v_{X,K}$, with the quotient tower and unit of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Denote by $\alpha^F_K:F_DK\to L_YF_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}K_\bullet$ the actual ambient ordinary-to-completed comparison after the counit-normalized identifications above.

The following identity holds naturally in every unbounded $K$:
$$\alpha^F_K=\beta_{K_\bullet}\,F_D(\operatorname{comp}_K).$$
Here $\alpha^F_K$ is the projection-defined K-injective/strict-augmentation map specified in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], rather than an arbitrary map to the limit object. If $p_n:L_YF_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}K_\bullet\to F_D(K_n)$ is its specified evaluation and $q_{n,K}:K\to K_n$ the quotient augmentation, then
$$p_n\alpha^F_K=F_D(q_{n,K}).$$
For every $m\ge n$, $F_D(\rho_{m,n})p_m=p_n$, where $\rho_{m,n}:K_m\to K_n$ is the strict quotient transition, and these identities respect composite quotient transitions. No completeness of $K$ or countable-product preservation by $F$ is assumed.

proof.text:
Write $H=F_D$, $\widetilde H=F_D^{\mathrm{Tow}}$, $M=K_\bullet$, and use right-to-left composition. Put $a_K=\widetilde H(i_K)j_K^{-1}:\Delta_YHK\to\widetilde HM$. The definition of completed pullback first applies pullback to the strict quotient augmentation and then applies the canonical constant-tower/derived-limit unit. Counit normalization identifies this pulled augmentation with $a_K$, on constant towers and on the entire quotient tower. Consequently the actual map is
$$\alpha^F_K=L_Y(a_K)v_{Y,HK}.$$
To check the normalization on representatives, take the flat-term K-flat representative $P$ used by that definition, its quotient tower $P_\bullet$, and a target K-injective tower resolution $r:F(P_\bullet)\to J_\bullet$. The actual construction is the chain map $FP\to\lim J_n$ whose components are $r_nF(P\to P_n)$. The canonical derived adjunction takes exactly this strict augmentation to that chain map: its unit factors the compatible component maps through the ordinary limit. Thus the displayed expression describes the specified map, including its resolution and localization comparisons. This uses the existing K-injective model for total right derived limit and the existing canonical derived adjunction; it does not assert that $F$ preserves K-injectives.

proof.text:
Set $h=\operatorname{comp}_K:K\to L_XM$. Expand the definition of $\beta_M$ and move $H(h)$ past $v_Y$ by its naturality. Naturality of $j^{-1}$ for $h$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_M H(h)
 &=L_Y\bigl(\widetilde H(\varepsilon_{X,M})j^{-1}_{L_XM}\Delta_YH(h)\bigr)v_{Y,HK}\\
 &=L_Y\bigl(\widetilde H(\varepsilon_{X,M}\Delta_Xh)j_K^{-1}\bigr)v_{Y,HK}.
\end{aligned}$$
The first move is $v_{Y,HL_XM}H(h)=L_Y\Delta_YH(h)v_{Y,HK}$, and the second is $j^{-1}_{L_XM}\Delta_YH(h)=\widetilde H(\Delta_Xh)j_K^{-1}$. These are substitutions of naturality and functoriality, with no preservation-of-limit assumption.

proof.text:
The source completion map is $h=L_X(i_K)v_{X,K}$. Counit naturality for $i_K:\Delta_XK\to M$ and the left triangle identity give
$$\begin{aligned}
\varepsilon_{X,M}\Delta_Xh
 &=\varepsilon_{X,M}\Delta_XL_X(i_K)\Delta_Xv_{X,K}\\
 &=i_K\varepsilon_{X,\Delta_XK}\Delta_Xv_{X,K}
 =i_K.
\end{aligned}$$
Substitution in Step 2 gives $\beta_M H(\operatorname{comp}_K)=L_Y(\widetilde H(i_K)j_K^{-1})v_{Y,HK}$, which equals $\alpha^F_K$ by Step 1. This is an equality of the actual morphisms in the derived category, obtained before evaluating any projection.

proof.text:
For the canonical target adjunction, the existing counit-projection theorem says $p_n=\operatorname{ev}_n(\varepsilon_{Y,\widetilde HM})$. The formula from Step 1 and counit naturality give
$$\varepsilon_{Y,\widetilde HM}\Delta_Y\alpha^F_K
 =\varepsilon_{Y,\widetilde HM}\Delta_YL_Y(a_K)\Delta_Yv_{Y,HK}
 =a_K\varepsilon_{Y,\Delta_YHK}\Delta_Yv_{Y,HK}=a_K.$$
Evaluate this identity at $n$. Since $\operatorname{ev}_n\Delta_Y=\mathrm{id}$, its left side is $p_n\alpha^F_K$. The counit-normalized exact evaluation comparison and $j$ identify its right side $\operatorname{ev}_n(a_K)$ with $H(q_{n,K})$. Hence $p_n\alpha^F_K=F_D(q_{n,K})$.

proof.text:
The target counit is a morphism in the derived strict tower category, so its evaluations commute with every evaluation transition. Its source is the constant tower on $L_Y\widetilde HM$, hence has identity transitions. Its target transition is $H(\rho_{m,n})$, by the termwise exact functor and its normalized evaluation identifications. Therefore $H(\rho_{m,n})p_m=p_n$ for all $m\ge n$. For $m\ge n\ge r$, the strict quotient law gives
$$H(\rho_{n,r})H(\rho_{m,n})p_m=H(\rho_{m,r})p_m=p_r;$$
for equal indices the transition is the identity. The quotient law here is induced by the coefficient quotient maps, whose composites are the direct quotient maps. Naturality in $K$ follows by applying the functors and natural transformations $i,j,v,\varepsilon$ to any morphism $K\to K'$; each displayed equality is an equality of their composites. All constructions are on unbounded derived categories. Neither invertibility of $\operatorname{comp}_K$ nor product preservation by $F$ was used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NK-b134eaaa9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS, no fixes. I read all five steps in full. This is an ordinary first split of an item that had no proof: NV created it unsplit in 9ae4c040, there is no repair note, the live copy is still unsplit, nothing cited is dropped, and no SGA source is used. The delivery adds no new nodes. Its only statement change adds lem-coef-derived-tower-counit-projections as the citation for the canonical adjunction Δ⊣Rlim. That is warranted, because the ringed-limit node gives only the K-injective model. The hypotheses and conclusions are unchanged, and the added dependency creates no cycle. Step 1 unwinds def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback and the α^F_K of lem-sf-exact-pullback-counit-normalization into L_Y(a_K)v_{Y,HK}, with a_K=H̃(i_K)j_K^{-1}. The definition's canonical map C→RlimΔC is the unit of the induced adjunction: Stacks Tag 0FND (derived.tex l.9517ff) builds the derived Hom bijection as the colimit over resolutions of the chain-level adjunct, so this is what the cited node states (C3 holds). Steps 2-3 are the mate/unit naturality and the triangle identity. I checked them, and they agree with the existing Mathlib leaf lem-pur-mate-unit-compatibility plus naturality of β. Citing that leaf would be optional and is not a fault. Step 4 gives ε_{H̃M}Δ_Y(α)=a_K, and evaluating at n with e_n(ε)=π_n gives p_nα=F_D(q_n). Step 5 uses naturality of the evaluation transitions on the counit morphism and the strict quotient composition law. I accept the tool uses of the ringed strict-tower limit and the derived-tower counit projections; both are generic category tools. Edge cases hold: g=id (β=id by the triangle identity), K=0, and the non-complete K=B[1/ℓ]. Mathlib searches cover all three kinds. None of the four mate and tower-normalization nodes I checked states this identity.

lean.statement: theorem completed_pullback_mate_factorization : (∀ K : DerivedCategory (pbcModules X (pbcAdicCompletion X d)), exactAugmentation d g K = (moduleFunctor d g).mapDerivedCategory.map (d.completionUnit X K) ≫ limitMate d g ((completedReductionTower X d).obj K)) ∧ (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (pbcModules X (pbcAdicCompletion X d))) (n : ℕ), exactAugmentation d g K ≫ pulledProjection d g n K = (moduleFunctor d g).mapDerivedCategory.map (quotientAugmentation d n K)) ∧ (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (pbcModules X (pbcAdicCompletion X d))) (a b : ℕ) (h : a ≤ b), pulledProjection d g b K ≫ (moduleFunctor d g).mapDerivedCategory.map (quotientTransition d a b h K) = pulledProjection d g a K) ∧ (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (pbcModules X (pbcAdicCompletion X d))) (a b c : ℕ) (hab : a ≤ b) (hbc : b ≤ c), pulledProjection d g c K ≫ (moduleFunctor d g).mapDerivedCategory.map (quotientTransition d b c hbc K) ≫ (moduleFunctor d g).mapDerivedCategory.map (quotientTransition d a b hab K) = pulledProjection d g c K ≫ (moduleFunctor d g).mapDerivedCategory.map (quotientTransition d a c (hab.trans hbc) K)) ∧ (∀ (K K' : DerivedCategory (pbcModules X (pbcAdicCompletion X d))) (f : K ⟶ K'), (moduleFunctor d g).mapDerivedCategory.map f ≫ exactAugmentation d g K' = exactAugmentation d g K ≫ (completedTowerRlim d Y).map ((towerFunctor d g).mapDerivedCategory.map ((completedReductionTower X d).map f)))
